1.
Proceedings in the present case arises from filing of DAR in FIR No.291/2017 of PS Jagat Puri regarding the accident in question.
Said FIR was registered by the injured/petitioner herein namely Vipin Sachdev.

As per petitioner on 04.10.2017 at about 11 p.m. he was going towards his home by his Scooty no. DL 5S-AS-1999 via road no.57 and when he reached near under construction metro station Krishna Nagar, offending MACT No.711/2017 Page 1 truck bearing registration no.
HR46C-2987 being driven by respondent no.1 in a rash and negligent manner as well as in a high speed struck the Scooty of the injured from back side.
Due to impact injured fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries including fracture of fibula left leg, degloving injury left leg.
Injured was taken to Dr.Hedgewar Hospital where from he got the treatment in Lok Nayak Hospital.

2. After filing of DAR, reply has been filed by respondent no.1 and 2 wherein the allegations regarding the manner in which accident has taken place has been simply denied and it is pleaded that accident has not been caused due to negligence of respondent no.1 in driving offending truck no.HR46C-2987.
It is pleaded that offending vehicle was duly insured with United India Insurance Company vide policy no. 1120843117P104540.

1 3.
Reply to the DAR has also been filed by Respondent no.3/insurance company wherein accident having been caused by negligent driving of respondent no.1 has been denied.
Objection has been taken that all the relevant documents including MLC result, medical treatment record and verified medical bills have not been annexed with the DAR.
Factum regarding offending vehicle being insured under the above mentioned policy for period from 27.06.2017 to 26.06.2018 has not been disputed.

It is pleaded that truck in question was goods carrying vehicle and since the accident involves two vehicle i.e. Scooty no.DL5S-AS-1999 as well offending truck no.HR-46C-2987,
therefore it is pleaded that petitioner is liable for contributory negligence.
Other facts have been denied.
4. On the basis of pleadings following issues were frame dby

ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal on 02.02.2018:
(1)Whether petitioner suffered injuries during the MACT No.711/2017 Page 2 accident occurred on 04.10.2017 at about 11.00 PM, in front of Krishna Nagar Metro Station, Road No.57, Delhi, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle bearing No.HR-46C 2984 being driven by respondent no.1/driver?
OPP (2)Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extend and from whom?
OPP (3)Relief.

5. Petitioner in order to substantiate his case has examined three witnesses i.e. PW1 petitioner Vipin Sachdeva, PW2 Dr.Dipankar Verma from GTB Hospital, who proved the permanent disability certificate of petitioner, PW3 Nandraj Singh from Income Tax Department proving ITR of petitioner.
6. No evidence has been led on behalf of respondent no.1 and 2 or on behalf of respondent no.3/insurance company.
7. I have heard Ms.Pooja Goel, ld. Counsel for the petitioner as well as Sh.S. Ghosh, ld. Counsel for respondent no.3/insurance company.
Issue No.1 8.
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided MACT No.711/2017 Page 3 on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.

In the facts of the present case petitioner/PW1 in his deposition has has specifically deposed that on 04.10.2017 when he was going towards his home on his Scooty no. DL-5S-AS-1999 from Vikram Dar - Vipin Sachdeva vs Ramesh on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115046735/
2 Singh Colony via road no.57 and when he reached near under construction Metro Station Krishna Nagar, truck no. HR-46C-2987 being driven in a rash and negligent manner and in a very high speed struck the scooty of petitioner from behind, resultantly petitioner along with his scooty fell down on the road and suffered multiple injuries.
10. In cross-examination of PW1 nothing came to disbelieve the version of accident as given by PW1.
Rather evidence of PW1 remained consistent on the aspect of accident, having been caused by rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 of truck no. HR-46C-2987.

Beside cogent evidence of PW1 documents annexed with DAR of FIR No.291/2017 of PS Jagat Puri, site plan of the place of accident also shows that the Scooty of the injured was struck from behind by the truck.

This fact gets corroboration from the mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle no. HR-46C-2987 which as per the documents annexed with the DAR was being driven by respondent no.1 Ramesh s/o Late Karan Singh.
Thus in view of cogent evidence of PW1 coupled with documents annexed with the DAR, this Tribunal finds that accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 only.
Accordingly issue stands decided in favour of petitioner and agains the respondents.
MACT No.711/2017 Page 4  Issue No.2 11.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant extract is as under:
"Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages.

Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss.

So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned,
they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit;
(iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort,
disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life."
12. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:
Dar - Vipin Sachdeva vs Ramesh on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115046735/

3 4. The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation MACT No.711/2017 Page 5 should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident.
The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.

The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.

This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.

5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following:
Pecuniary Damages (special damages)

(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,
nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure.

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising:
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment.
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages)
(iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.
(v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage)
(vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity).
In routine personal injury cases, compensation will MACT No.711/2017 Page 6 be awarded only under heads (i), (ii), (a) and (iv).

It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss Dar - Vipin Sachdeva vs Ramesh on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115046735/
4 of expectation of life.

13. In the light of the aforementioned judgments, the compensation to which the petitioner is entitled shall be as under:-
PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Medical Expenses:
14.

PW1 in his evidence has stated that immediately after the accident he was brought to Hedgewar Hospital on 04.10.2017 and since his condition was very critical due to the injuries suffered in accident, he was referred to Lok Nayak Hospital, where he was admitted on 05.10.2017 and discharged on 25.11.2017 with advise of the doctor for complete bed rest.

PW1 testified as well as medical documents proved in his deposition establish that petitioner suffered grievous injuries including fracture of fibula left leg, degloving injury left leg beside other injuries.

Medical condition of the petitioner was assessed by Medical Board of GTB Hospital, which issued the permanent disability certificate no.637/53/06/18 dated 12.06.2018 wherein medical board found that petitioner suffered 67% of permanent disability in relation to left lower limb.
15.
PW1 proved treatment record Ex.PW1/5 along with medical bills/pharmacy bills Ex.PW1/2.
Evidently the entire treatment (including inward/outward patient) of petitioner has been in government hospital where petitioner had not to spent anything, beside medicine expenses.
The MACT No.711/2017 Page 7 total of pharmacy bills placed on record Ex.PW1/2 comes out to be Rs.1,362/-.

This Tribunal is conscious of the fact that beside the bills placed on the record, there may be certain bills either misplaced or for other reasons could not be brought on record and petitioner must have spent more amount towards the medical/pharmacy expenses.

As such taking into consideration the nature of injuries, permanent disability suffered by the petitioner, this Tribunal conclude medical expenses to the tune of Rs.5,000/- as treatment of the petitioner has been in government hospital.
Loss of earning during treatment:
16. PW1 in his affidavit has testified that he was running a printing press with the name M/s Sachdeva Packers and was earning around Rs.3,05,840/- per annum as per his income tax return.
PW1 in order to prove his monthly/annual income has referred to his ITR 2015-16, 2016-17 and 2017-18, collectively exhibited as Ex.PW1/4.
Beside this petitioner has also examined PW3 Nand Raj Singh from IT Department who proved certified copy of ITR of petitioner for assessment year 2015-16.
As per the said ITR the gross annual income of the petitioner is Rs.2,78,950/-.

As per the ITR of assessment year 2016-17, the gross income of petitioner is mentioned as Rs.2,94,580/- and as per the ITR for assessment year 2017-18 gross income of the petitioner is Rs.3,05,840/-.
17.

Thus taking into consideration the above referred ITRs of the petitioner, more particularly last and relevant ITR of assessment year 2017- 18, this Tribunal concludes the annual income of the petitioner to be Rs.3,05,840/- i.e. Rs.25,487/- per month.

Dar - Vipin Sachdeva vs Ramesh on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115046735/
5 18.
From the medical record proved in the evidence of PW1, petitioner remained hospitalized for about two months i.e. from 04.10.2017 MACT No.711/2017 Page 8 to 25.11.2017.
There are also documents showing that even after discharge, petitioner continued taking treatment as OPD patient in Lok Nayak Hospital.

Thus taking into consideration the period of hospitalization, period of OPD treatment and nature of injuries i.e. multiple grievous injuries including fracture of fibula left leg,
this Tribunal finds that petitioner suffered loss of income due to treatment for about 04 months.
As such petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,01,948/- (Rs.25,487 X 4) under this head.

Loss of future earning due to disability :
19.

In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:-
"9.
Therefore, the Tribunal has to first decide whether there is any permanent disability and if so, the extent of such permanent disability.
If the Tribunal concludes that there is no permanent MACT No.711/2017 Page 9 disability then there is no question of proceeding further and determining the loss of future earning capacity.
But if the Tribunal concludes that there is permanent disability then it will proceed to ascertain its extent.

After the Tribunal ascertains the actual extent of permanent disability of the claimant based on the medical evidence, it has to determine whether such permanent disability has affected or will affect his earning capacity.
10.
Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps.

The tribunal has to first ascertain what activities of the claimant could carry on in spite of the permanent disability and what he could not do as a result of permanent disability (this is also relevant for awarding compensation under the head of loss of amenities of life).
The second step is to ascertain his avocation, profession and nature of work before the accident, as also his age.

The third step is to find out whether (i) the claimant is totally disabled from earning any kind of livelihood or (ii) whether in spite of the permanent disability, the claimant could still effectively carry on the activities and functions, which he was earlier carrying on, or (iii) Whether he was Dar - Vipin Sachdeva vs Ramesh on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115046735/
6 prevented or restricted from discharging his previous activities and functions so that he continues to earn or can continue to earn his livelihood."
....If doctor has given evidence about percentage of permanent disability, Tribunal will have to seek doctors opinion as to whether it is possible to deduce the corresponding functional permanent disability with reference to whole body and if so to what percentage.

13. We may now summarize the principles discussed above:
(i). All injuries (or permanent disabilities arising from injuries), do not result in loss of earning capacity.
MACT No.711/2017 Page 10
(ii). The percentage of permanent disability with reference to the whole body of a person, cannot be assumed to be the percentage of loss of earning capacity.

To put it differently, the percentage of loss of earning capacity is not the same as the percentage of permanent disability (except in a few cases, where the Tribunal on the basis of evidence, concludes that percentage of loss of earning capacity is the same as percentage of permanent disability).

(iii). The doctor who treated an injured- claimant or who examined him subsequently to assess the extent of his permanent disability can give evidence only in regard the extent of permanent disability.
The loss of earning capacity is something that will have to be assessed by the Tribunal with reference to the evidence in entirety.

(iv). The same permanent disability may result in different percentages of loss of earning capacity in different persons, depending upon the nature of profession,
occupation or job, age, education and other factors."
20.

Keeping in view the ratio as discussed above, in the present case it is evident on record that as a result of the injuries sustained by petitioner in an accident, he suffered 67% of permanent disability in relation to left lower limb.
It came in the deposition of PW1 as well as other medical documents proved on the record that petitioner got the treatment of his injuries in above mentioned hospitals.

PW2 Dr.Dipankar Verma who proved the disability certificate of petitioner stated in his cross-examination that patient would face difficulty in ankle movement, as he suffered injuries in his ankle and would also suffer difficulty in long standing, walking on slope, stairs, however can do any job of sitting.
PW2 further stated that petitioner's injuries were found to be permanent in nature.
Now question arises how much 67% of the permanent medical disability has effected on MACT No.711/2017 Page 11 the functional ability of petitioner.

21. Hon'ble Apex Court in the matter of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (supra) has laid down that Tribunal is bound to assess the evidence on the record, for the purpose of ascertaining the functional disability of the petitioner on account of medical permanent disability to assess how much the medical disability adversely affected on the functional capacity of the petitioner/injured so that just Dar - Vipin Sachdeva vs Ramesh on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115046735/
7 and fair amount of compensation can be ascertained under the heading of future loss of earning.
22. It came in the deposition of PW1 that he was working as a businessman by running a printing press by name M/s Sachdeva Packers.

Being a self employed/proprietor businessman, it is very much obvious that petitioner had to move to different places for taking orders and also to ensure delivery of his printing press material and therefore petitioner would certainly suffer functional disability on account of the permanent disability suffered by him in an accident.

As such taking into consideration the nature of work of petitioner involving his regular movement, this Tribunal assess functional disability of petitioner to the extent of 40% vis a vis permanent medical disability of 67%.
23. Further, law is well settled that there should be no departure from the multiplier method in injury cases also [refer: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351].

entities.text: Sandeep Khanuja vs. Atul Dande & Anr., (2017) 3 SCC 351
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the DL of petitioner Ex.PW1/6, date of birth of the petitioner is found to be 11.09.1971.
As such at the time of accident petitioner was 46 years of age.

As such multiplier to be applied in the present case would be 13 as applicable to age group between 46 to 50 years, would be applicable as per settled principle laid down in case of Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121.

Moreover, the law has been well settled by the decisions of Supreme Court in the MACT No.711/2017 Page 12 cases of Sandeep Khanuja (supra) and Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., 2020 SCC OnLine SC 601,
that while applying the multiplier method, future prospects on advancement in life and career are also to be taken into consideration.

entities.text: Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., 2020 SCC OnLine SC 601
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, considering the petitioner being below the age of 50 years at the time of accident and was self employed, in view of the judgment in Pranay Sethi & Others (supra) an addition of income to the extent of 25% towards future prospects has to be counted.

24. As discussed above, the income of petitioner has been assessed as Rs.25,487 + 25% (Rs.6,372/-),
total Rs.31,859/- (Rs.25,487 + Rs.6,372).
Thus applying the functional disability to be 40% of Rs.31,859/-, amount comes out to be Rs.12,744/-.
As such the loss of future income due to disability comes out to be Rs.12,744/- X 12 X 13 = Rs.19,88,064/-.
Special Diet & Conveyance Charges:
25. Petitioner (PW1) in his evidence by way of affidavit deposed that he has already spent huge amount on conveyance amounting to Rs.35,000/-.
PW1 also deposed that he was forced to take high and rich protein diet for early recovery of health and for this he spent extra amount of Rs.30,000/-.

Though petitioner has proved on record his medical treatment documents, but no documentary evidence in the form of prescription of doctor or bills of transportation and special diet has been placed on record to substantiate her claim that he has incurred any expenses towards conveyance and special diet.

In the absence of any such documentary proof, this Tribunal while taking into consideration period of hospitalization of petitioner, seriousness of injuries suffered by him, finds it appropriate to grant compensation for a sum of Rs.25,000/- towards conveyance charges and a sum of Rs.35,000/- towards special diet.
MACT No.711/2017 Page 13  Attendant Charges:
26. On the question of nursing attendant, PW1 in his deposition has stated that he incurred expenditure for keeping an attendant and paid sum of Rs.8,000/- per month.

Although no documentary evidence in this regard has been placed on record but taking into consideration nature Dar - Vipin Sachdeva vs Ramesh on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115046735/
8 of injuries and permanent disability to the extent of 67% in relation to left lower limb and the fact that petitioner must have taken treatment for about 04 months, petitioner is given attendant charges on the basis of minimum wages of an unskilled worker prevalent in Delhi in October 2017 which were Rs.13,584/- per month.

Thus total amount of compensation under this head comes out to be Rs.54,336/- (Rs.13,584/- X 4).
NON PECUNIARY DAMAGES :
Pain & Sufferings:
27. While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victim of vehicular accident

, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No:
709/02, date of decision: 02.02.2007 can be considered:
"12.
On account of pain and suffering, suffice would it be to note that it is difficult to measure pain and suffering in terms of a money value.
However, compensation which has to be paid must bear some objectives co-relation with the pain and suffering.

13. The objective facts relatable to pain and suffering would be:
(a) Nature of injury.
(b) Body part affected (c) Duration of the treatment."
28.
In this case, as per medical documents of the petitioner, he was found to have suffered multiple injuries on his body.

His treatment record including medical disability certificate shows he sustained medical MACT No.711/2017 Page 14 permanent disability in relation to his left lower limb and remained hospitalized for about two months and discharged from hospital on 25.11.2017.

Thus,
it is clear that petitioner must have suffered immense pain and suffering during his treatment and therefore, this Tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of Rs.1,00,000/- would be just and fair compensation for pain, sufferings and mental trauma suffered by the petitioner as consequences of injuries sustained in the accident.
Accordingly, Rs.1,00,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.
29. Ld. counsel for petitioner submitted that petitioner is entitled for compensation on account of disfigurement to the tune of Rs.50,000/-.
Ld. counsel further submitted that due to injuries suffered by petitioner, he has also being deprived of his marital enjoyment and therefore is liable to be compensated on those counts.

Dar - Vipin Sachdeva vs Ramesh on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115046735/
9 30.

Having considered the submissions there is no denial to the fact that petitioner suffered permanent disability to the extent of 67% but it is also matter of record that petitioner has been given treatment and had recovered from fracture.

This Tribunal has already taken into account entire facts and circumstances including medical difficulties and permanent disability certificate of the petitioner while awarding compensation for pain and suffering.
As such compensation on account of disfigurement, loss of marital pleasure etc. is very much inclusive in the compensation awarded under pain and suffering.
Loss of Amenities:

31. Having considered the evidence of PW1, PW2 proving disability certificate, once it has already come on the record that petitioner suffered injuries to his lower left limb, this Tribunal has already noted that petitioner being at prime of his age pursuing for his business, independently, therefore MACT No.711/2017 Page 15 must have lost certain amenities of life on account of injuries suffered in the accident.
Therefore taking into consideration nature of injury as well as the fact that petitioner was pursuing his business, he is awarded a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- under the head of loss of amenities.

32. Thus, the compensation awarded to the petitioner is summarized as under:-

. Thus, the total compensation amount to which the petitioner is entitled comes to Rs.24,09,348/-.

Petitioner shall also be entitled to interest @ 8% per annum on the award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.

Now, the question arises as to which of the respondent is liable to pay the compensation amount.
It is an admitted fact that the offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no.3/insurance company.

In view of my findings on above issues, it is held that respondent no.3/ insurance Dar - Vipin Sachdeva vs Ramesh on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/115046735/

Amount of interim award, if any, be deducted from the compensation amount along with the waiver of interest, if any, as directed by the Tribunal during the pendency of this case.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the settled proposition of law that an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v.
Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided MACT No.711/2017 Page 3 on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi & Others v. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018, Law Suit (SC) 303.
9.
Thus in view of cogent evidence of PW1 coupled with documents annexed with the DAR, this Tribunal finds that accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.1 only.
The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755.
12. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases.

The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable.
A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury.
This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned.
Thus taking into consideration the period of hospitalization, period of OPD treatment and nature of injuries i.e. multiple grievous injuries including fracture of fibula left leg,
